title: External target sidecar (authored work manifest)
description: What a real-world example's target.json states about the external change it scaffolds: its identity, its history, how its artifacts are prepared, its tasks, its controls and its handoff. It is a work manifest, not a specification language: a claim, model, contract or witness file is referred to by path (and hashed where it is pinned), never restated. An example opts in with `"target": "target.json"` in its example.json, which only a real-world example may have. examples/tools/targets/sidecar.py validates it against this schema and then makes the checks a schema can't: every path stays inside the example's folder, every revision, pair and task named is defined, and task prerequisites have no cycle. Frozen by Phase 0 of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md; from then on the workflow stream owns it, with additive changes recorded for the merge. Readiness and proof outcomes are not stored here: they are derived from the receipts.

schema.description: The sidecar's version. Another version is refused, never read as this one.

case.description: The stable logical case id, as the seed file names it (not the example number).

family.description: The family the case belongs to; a negative and its independent positive share it.

role.description: negative: a vulnerability's vulnerable and fixed revisions; positive: an independent accepted change with an expected outcome for a named claim (never 'the release is secure'); calibration: a supported obligation that checks the route itself (105); catalog: research metadata only, no deep build; control: a constructed sensitivity case.

companions.description: Related examples by number: a negative's positive, a follow-up CVE.

matching.description: Why a companion is matched, and where the match is imperfect.

sourceConfidence.description: researched: taken from earlier research, not yet checked; checked-upstream: every revision checked against the upstream repository; reproduced: the revisions were built or fetched and replayed.

cve.description: The CVE id, for a negative or catalog entry.

repository.description: The upstream repository, on github.com (the downloads policy of decision 1).

researchedOn.description: When the research this entry comes from was done (the archived registry's as_of).

revisions.description: Each revision the case uses, by name. A commit is a full 40-hex SHA: a branch, a short SHA or a tag alone is a mutable reference and is refused. A tag or release is recorded beside the commit, never instead of it. A control (identity.role) may instead name a `fixture`: a directory of sources in its folder, built locally, never an upstream revision. A constructed `mutant` (any role) is another revision with a patch applied: it stays constructed, never an upstream change, a CVE or a historical success.

route.description: This revision's own route, where it differs from preparation.route: on the source-slice route only, a published release that carries a slice revision's sources (its JAR, then its dependencies, in preparation.artifacts), compared with that slice revision in a `correspondence` pair.

fixture.description: For a control only: the revision's sources, a directory in the folder.

fixtureClasspath.description: Java source roots compiled into distinct dependency JARs and loaded in this exact order after the fixture.

compileLibraries.description: Library catalog entries on the client compiler's classpath, in order.

runtimeLibraries.description: Library catalog entries loaded after the unchanged client, in order.

orderedClasses.description: Dependency classes intentionally provided by multiple fixture JARs. The first provider supplies the class. The preparation records every contender and its class digest.

fixtureCompiler.description: JDK and compiler flags for this revision's original subject.

mutant.description: A constructed mutation control (added by the workflow stream, additive): the revision `base` with the patch `patch` applied, its sha256 checked before anything is prepared from it. Its base is a commit or fixture revision of this sidecar, and it appears only as the `after` of a `mutation` pair whose `before` is that base. It has no upstream identity: no parent, tag or release, and no published artifact.

base.description: A revision name: what the patch applies to.

patch.description: A unified diff in the folder, applied in the base's source root.

description.description: The mutation in words: what it changes, and which branch or observation it is meant to break.

parent.description: The parent this case compares against; for a merge commit, the selected one.

parentReason.description: Why that parent was selected, for a merge commit.

checked.description: How the commit (and its parent) was checked against upstream, and when.

pairs.description: Separately named revision pairs: a release comparison, the exact fix, an introduction, a positive change, a constructed mutation, a correspondence (a slice revision against a published build of the same sources: both sides must show the same problems, on every JDK). A fix's parent is never an introduction by default.

selected.description: The pair executed, chosen explicitly before a claim is frozen.

links.description: Patches, pull requests, issues and other sources.

status.description: unknown; candidate: a source-level hypothesis; vendor-attributed: the vendor says so, unreproduced; established: a reproduced parent/child transition with an independent oracle.

preparation.description: How the artifacts are obtained. Absent while the case is only catalogued.

route.description: published-artifact: specific JARs from Maven Central or repo.spring.io, checksums checked; upstream-build: the exact commit built with its own build tool and a JDK it supports; source-slice: named source files of each exact commit compiled alone, by a pinned JDK and javac flags, against pinned published JARs (`slice`), an extracted source slice: a narrower scope than the commit's own build, labelled so in every receipt; fixture: a control's fixture revisions, built locally (Phase 0's examples/tools/targets/fixtures/build_fixtures.py).

artifacts.description: Per revision, in classpath order: on the published-artifact route the revision's own JAR first, then its dependencies; on the source-slice route the JARs its slice is compiled against and run with.

coordinates.description: group:artifact:version, a fixed version: a range, `+`, LATEST, RELEASE or a SNAPSHOT is refused.

url.description: Where it is fetched from: Maven Central, repo.spring.io or github.com only (runtime_maven.py's policy decides).

sha256.description: Recorded the first time it is fetched, checked on every reuse.

tool.description: The revision's own build tool, by its wrapper where it has one.

argv.description: The exact argument vector, run in the checkout's root.

slice.description: The source-slice route's recipe: which files of each revision's checkout are compiled, and how. A mutant compiles its base's files, patched.

files.description: Per revision name, the paths of the Java sources compiled together, from the repository's root; nothing else of the checkout is compiled.

jdk.description: The JDK whose javac compiles the slice.

companionClasses.description: Additional package-private top-level classes expected from the listed Java sources. Each class must identify one of those files in its SourceFile attribute.

flags.description: javac's flags, in order, from -g, -g:none, -g:{source,lines,vars}, -parameters, -source N, -target N, --release N and -encoding NAME only (runtime checks them).

matches.description: Per revision name (one the slice compiles), published classes its compiled slice must reproduce byte for byte: the class, its sha256 as an entry of the published JAR, and that JAR, fetched by its own sha256 when the revision is prepared. A mismatch fails the preparation (a blocker); the slice is never used anyway. A mutant inherits none of its base's.

class.description: The class's entry name in the JAR, as javac writes it under the slice's output directory.

jar.description: The published JAR that carries the class.

jdks.description: The JDKs the concrete controls run on, each a separate identity (21 and 25 wherever the artifacts run on them).

capturedBuilds.description: Full upstream build records, by revision. Restoring their hash-checked products avoids rebuilding a dependency for every claim.

libraryCatalog.description: JSON file of pinned Maven releases or full upstream build recipes used by a client fixture.

adapters.description: Adapter sources in the example's folder, compiled separately from the original sources.

tasks.description: Each task a later agent can plan, prepare, run or hand off. Empty for a catalog entry. A repair is composed from separate tasks (the vulnerable property, the same property on the fix, preservation); there is no fix task.

kind.description: prove: a property of one revision; compare or equivalence: two revisions of a pair; replay: concrete controls only, on one revision or a pair's two.

revision.description: A revision name, for prove and replay.

pair.description: A pair name, for compare and equivalence.

claim.description: The claim file in the folder (claims/), once written; it is frozen before the attempt.

expected.description: The authored semantic expectation, never rewritten after a result: refuted (the vulnerable property), established (the fix, preservation), or unresolved.

allowedChange.description: For a preservation or compatibility task: the inputs the change is allowed to affect, a Java boolean expression over the method's parameters (B9's intendedInputs). It is justified before any attempt and never enlarged after a counterexample.

requires.description: Prerequisite tasks, by id. A cycle is refused.

parent.description: For a narrower diagnostic or derived claim: the task it is derived from, which stays unresolved.

engine.description: Named explicitly: native strict is the default this wave asks for, and the CLI's default engine is JBMC.

checkedLemmas.description: Local lemma declarations that the native checker must prove at this task's bounds before using them. This selects a proof strategy for the same source claim.

bounds.description: Explicit bounds, by the tool's option names (maxArrayLength, unwind, maxStringLength ...).

besideRoute.description: An answer to this task's claim given beside the route: by a script of the example's own, on the claim file as frozen, run as a verification job, which leaves no receipt. llm-dlc/tools/changes.py counts the claim as decided only while the acceptance check (examples/tools/accept.py) derives this answer from what that job left: its result in the checkout, passed and naming the example (links.examples), and the outcome its step wrote giving this verdict about the claim as frozen, at the claim's bound; a route receipt, once there is one, outranks it. Written once the job is in; the task's `expected` and its claim stay as they were.

job.description: The verification job that gave it, by id (verification/jobs, verification/results).

by.description: How it was run and why not by the route, in a line: the script and what it adds (an adapter entry, a lemma).

invocation.description: How this task's proof is invoked, which the setup confirms without attempting the proof (llm-dlc/runtime.md, stage 3). route: the standard route (build.py) takes the task as it stands. adapter: a driver or adapter of the example's own enters the claim, compiled and run once on the prepared revisions, beside the route as example 286's proofs/prove.py does. gap: the verifier can't be given the task until a named capability is added, which an observed blocker of this task in the handoff records, with the claim kept as it is.

checked.description: The date the setup confirmed it.

evidence.description: What showed it: the task's plan and the entry resolved, the adapter compiled and run, or the blocker's probe.

entry.description: For adapter: the adapter's class and method, and the script that runs it.

blocker.description: For gap: the blocker's kind, as handoff.blockers names it.

controls.description: The independent oracle, the known trigger, legitimate inputs, mutation controls and replay drivers, as files in the folder.

kind.description: The capability-gap kinds of the brief, kept apart. verifier-interface: the verifier can't be given the task as stated, because its command line has no way to say it (equivalence's one --classpath for a pair with two dependency closures), though the inputs and the code are within what it checks; not an input it can't construct.

observed.description: true: a probe or attempt produced it; false: predicted, a hypothesis until a probe reaches it.

task.description: The task it blocks. Omitted: the whole target's, which applies to every task, a capability kind only to the tasks that run the verifier.

summary.description: Kept as it was written, even when a later attempt changes the packet's state: a predicted group on examples/gap-inventory.md is named by its kind and summary.

recorded.description: The date the summary was written.

note.description: A later line, opening with its own date ('YYYY-MM-DD: ...'), that says what changed since the summary was written, such as the observed blockers an attempt met first, and leaves the summary as it was.

packet.description: The gap packet's file in the folder.

finding.description: An existing finding id it reuses.

next.description: The one recommended next action, as an exact command where there is one.

jdk.description: A Temurin feature release installed under sdkman.

file.description: A path relative to the example's folder: no leading slash, no `..` segment, no backslash. sidecar.py also checks that it resolves inside the folder.
